question: How many passengers are in the dataset, and how many of them survived?

checks.description: Number of passengers
Number of survivors

question: Did women survive at a higher rate than men? Give the survival rate of each group.

checks.description: Survival rate of women, in percent
Survival rate of men, in percent
States the number of women and the number of men the rates are based on

question: What is the average age of the passengers?
traps: Age is missing for some passengers; the average must be computed over known ages and the missing count stated

checks.description: Mean age over passengers with a known age, in years
Number of passengers with a missing age
Does not give an average that counts missing ages as zero or that fills them in without saying so

question: Did passengers who survived pay more for their tickets than those who did not? Is the difference statistically significant?
traps: Fares are strongly right-skewed: the mean is far above the median, so medians or a rank-based test fit better than means alone

checks.description: Median fare of survivors
Median fare of those who died
Names the statistical test used, says what it compares (means, medians or distributions) and reports its p-value
Says that fares are skewed or that the mean and median differ a lot
Does not claim that paying more caused passengers to survive

question: What are the total sales of each product category? Rank the categories from highest to lowest.

checks.description: Categories by total sales, highest first
Total sales of Technology

question: Which three months had the highest sales in 2017? Give their sales.
traps: October and December 2017 are close; the ranking must follow the computed values

checks.description: Top three months of 2017 by sales, highest first
Sales in November 2017
Does not claim that October 2017 had higher sales than December 2017

question: Which product category has the highest profit margin, defined as total profit divided by total sales? Rank all categories.
traps: The two leading categories are close; an average of per-order margins gives a different order than the ratio of totals

checks.description: Categories by profit margin (total profit / total sales), highest first
Profit margin of Technology, in percent

question: Which region has the lowest profit margin (total profit divided by total sales), and which sub-category loses the most money in that region?

checks.description: Region with the lowest profit margin
Profit margin of that region, in percent
Sub-category with the largest total loss in that region
Total profit of that sub-category in that region (a negative number)

question: How many distinct customers made at least one purchase? Do not count cancellations as purchases.
traps: Many rows have no Customer ID and must not be counted as a customer

checks.description: Distinct customer IDs with at least one non-cancelled invoice
Says that rows without a Customer ID were left out

notes: abs_tol 5 covers the variant that defines a purchase as Quantity > 0 and Price > 0 instead of a non-'C' invoice (3 fewer customers).

question: Did net revenue grow from 2010 to 2011? Use Quantity x Price over all rows, including returns, after removing exact duplicate rows.
traps: The data ends on 9 December 2011, so 2011 is incomplete; comparing full 2010 with partial 2011 wrongly shows a decline

checks.description: Growth of net revenue from 2010 to 2011 on comparable periods, in percent
Says that the 2011 data ends on 9 December 2011 and adjusts the comparison for it
Does not conclude that revenue declined from 2010 to 2011

notes: The reference compares 1 January - 9 December of both years. abs_tol 2.5 points also covers the other reasonable adjustment, revenue per day of data (about 2 points higher).

question: What was the net revenue in 2010? Compute it as Quantity x Price over all rows, including cancellations and returns, after removing exact duplicate rows.
traps: The data has exact duplicate rows

checks.description: Net revenue in 2010 after removing exact duplicates
Number of exact duplicate rows removed (whole dataset)

question: Does monthly income differ between employees who left and those who stayed? Is the difference statistically significant?
traps: Income is right-skewed; medians or a rank-based test fit better than means alone

checks.description: Median monthly income of employees who left
Median monthly income of employees who stayed
Number of employees who left
Number of employees who stayed
Names the statistical test, says what it compares and reports its p-value
Reports an effect size: the size of the difference in money or percent, or a standardized measure

question: What is the attrition rate in each department? Rank the departments from highest to lowest.
traps: One department is much smaller than the others, so its rate is less certain

checks.description: Departments by attrition rate, highest first
Attrition rate of the top department, in percent
States the number of employees in each department or flags that one department is small

question: Among employees who work overtime, what share left the company? How does that compare with employees who do not work overtime?

checks.description: Attrition rate of employees who work overtime, in percent
Attrition rate of employees who do not work overtime, in percent
Does not claim that overtime causes employees to leave

question: Which year had the highest average temperature?
traps: The last year in the data has only one day; it must not be compared with full years

checks.description: Warmest year by mean temperature, among complete years
Mean temperature of that year
Says that the last year has only one day of data and was left out or treated separately
Does not rank the one-day year as the coldest or warmest year

question: What is the average daily mean air pressure in the data?
traps: The pressure column contains physically impossible values that distort the mean

checks.description: Mean pressure after excluding physically impossible values (hPa)
Says that some pressure values are impossible and how they were handled
Does not give the average that includes the impossible values as the answer

notes: The reference keeps 900-1100 hPa. abs_tol 0.5 covers other reasonable cleaning rules (950-1050 hPa, the IQR rule) and reporting the median instead.

question: Do patients with heart disease have different cholesterol levels from patients without it? Use an appropriate statistical test.
traps: Cholesterol is 0 for many patients, which means 'not measured'; these rows must be excluded

checks.description: Median cholesterol of patients with heart disease, zeros excluded
Median cholesterol of patients without heart disease, zeros excluded
Number of rows with cholesterol 0
Says that cholesterol 0 means a missing measurement and that those rows were excluded
Names the statistical test, says what it compares and reports its p-value

question: What percentage of male patients and of female patients have heart disease?

checks.description: Share of male patients with heart disease, in percent
Share of female patients with heart disease, in percent

question: Did the number of house sales in May 2015 drop compared with May 2014?
traps: The data ends before the end of May 2015, so May 2015 is incomplete and must be compared over the same days

checks.description: Number of sales in May 2015 (all days in the data)
Number of sales in May 2014 up to the same day of the month as the last day of May 2015 in the data
Says that May 2015 is incomplete (the data ends before the end of the month) and compares the same days or per-day rates
Does not conclude that sales dropped by comparing all of May 2014 with the incomplete May 2015

question: What is the typical sale price of a house in this data?
traps: Prices are strongly right-skewed; the median describes a typical sale better than the mean

checks.description: Median sale price
Explains that the mean is higher than the median because of a few very expensive houses
Does not present the mean as the typical price without mentioning the skew

question: Among zipcodes with at least 100 sales, which three have the highest median price per square foot of living area (price divided by sqft_living)?

checks.description: Zipcodes by median price per square foot, highest first
Median price per square foot of the first zipcode
